topic: Why America and Israel lost despite having a larger military budget than Iran

lines.text: Despite outspending Iran, the United States and Israel face unexpected setbacks in the Gulf.
lines.search_term: US and Israeli naval vessels near Strait of Hormuz

lines.text: Iran's strategic control of the Hormuz Strait threatens the flow of global oil.
lines.search_term: busy shipping lane in Strait of Hormuz with Iranian patrol boats

lines.text: Washington's reliance on costly military bases stretches its resources thin.
lines.search_term: American military base desert landscape with aircraft

lines.text: Israel's heavy aid from America cannot offset Iran's asymmetric tactics.
lines.search_term: Israeli defense forces training with US equipment in desert

lines.text: The recent Oman and Iran agreement forces the US and Israel to negotiate for passage.
lines.search_term: diplomatic meeting between Omani and Iranian officials

lines.text: Iran's reshuffled command signals a hardline stance that complicates diplomatic options.
lines.search_term: Iranian military leaders in briefing room with maps

lines.text: Economic sanctions and compensation demands add pressure on American shipping.
lines.search_term: cargo ship waiting near Hormuz under Iranian flag

lines.text: The US military's global commitments dilute its focus on the regional threat.
lines.search_term: US warships scattered across world map illustration

lines.text: Israel's reliance on US technology makes it vulnerable when supply lines are blocked.
lines.search_term: Israeli missile defense system on coastal hill with US flag overlay

lines.text: Ultimately, budget size alone cannot guarantee victory against Iran's localized advantage.
